summary: Intermittent client timeouts for very large max_tokens caused by prefetch + memory-slab thrashing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring timeouts (504 / client disconnect) when requesting very large max_tokens (>= 200k) with deep conversational history. Failures appear after 60-90s of generation and are intermittent across identical requests.

Impact:
- LexiDocs automated summarization pipelines fail to finalize outputs for ~5-15% of large-batch jobs during business hours.
- Customer sees elevated 504s and occasional streaming disconnects, impacting SLAs and downstream processing.

Environment:
- Prod cluster in us-east backed by Dedicated capacity (reserved pool).
- Traffic routed through api-gw-redwood-prod -> serving-runtime pool S-3 (GPU A100-like).
- KV cache enabled with prefix caching and prefetching turned on.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use customer prompt bundle with ~180k prompt tokens + request max_tokens: 40k, temperature 0.2, stream: true.
2) Send requests at ~2 QPS from LexiDocs client using API key tied to dedicated capacity.
3) Observe generation proceed for ~50-80s, then client receives 504 or stream closes with "connection reset by peer".
4) Retry same request immediately; often succeeds, sometimes fails again.

Expected behavior:
- Long-running generation should either complete within platform SLOs or fail with informative retryable error; streaming should remain connected while runtime is processing.

Actual behavior:
- Intermittent timeouts and stream disconnects after prolonged token generation; failures correlate with elevated memory allocator churn and increased prefetch latency in serving nodes.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- serving-runtime node srv-120: "WARN kernel_allocator: slab_reclaim(2048) delayed 120ms, prefetched_kv_misses=72"
- scheduler logs: "INFO batch-evict: dropped job SUP-100483-cust-lexidocs-394; reason=priority_starvation"
- api-gateway: "ERROR stream: upstream reset after 62s, client=lexidocs-prod-ip"

Attachments: customer sample prompt (redacted), request IDs: req_us-east_20260308_82a9, req_us-east_20260309_11d4
comments: 2026-03-08 - Support (Maya Chen): Initial report received from LexiDocs. Captured request IDs and requested environment details. Escalated to SRE due to P1 impact and SLA risk.

2026-03-09 - SRE (Rafael Ortega): Confirmed repeated 504s on listed request IDs. Observed slab reclaim spikes and prefetch miss bursts on serving nodes serving dedicated pool. Added 'blocking' label and pausing customer retries to gather traces.

2026-03-10 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Hypothesis: KV prefetch + large contiguous prefix allocations cause allocator fragmentation and GC-like slab thrash under sustained long-token generation. Looking at disabling prefetch for reproducer window. Created internal run INT-4543.

2026-03-11 - Support (Maya Chen) -> Customer: Temporary mitigation: lower max_tokens to 20k or gate through batch size reduction. Customer testing confirms reduced failure rate at 20k. Asked for permission to toggle prefetch on dedicated pool for a short test.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Rafael Ortega): Performed targeted A/B change: disabled KV prefetch on one serving node (srv-120). Re-ran reproduced workflow; observed stable memory allocator behavior and no stream resets for 12 runs. Will monitor for 24h and propose patch.
2026-03-12 - Customer (LexiDocs Engineer - Aaron Patel): Confirmed improved success on test node. Asking for ETA on full fix and whether this will affect latency/cost.

2026-03-12 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Draft patch to make prefetch adaptive to prefix and memory headroom (PR linked). Preparing canary rollout and a tuning parameter for enterprise customers. Estimated rollout to staging in 2 days, prod in 7 days pending validation.
investigation_notes: Prefetcher triggers synchronous KV loads for contiguous large prefix ranges; these loads compete with token generation for GPU and CPU worker threads, increasing latency and causing allocator slab reclaim cycles.
Memory profiler snapshots show high fragmentation and >40% increase in malloc/reclaim rate during failing runs versus successful runs.
Scheduler trace shows priority inversion: background prefetch jobs were enqueued with equal priority to active generation tasks, causing eviction of active jobs in edge conditions.
Reproducer validated on dedicated pool nodes with customer payloads; disabling prefetch eliminated failures in test window.
Potential contributing factor: recent kernel allocator change in commit 6f2d3 altered slab bucket thresholds, making long contiguous allocations more likely to trigger reclaim.
Risk assessment: wholesale disabling of prefetch may increase tail latency for some workloads and could increase token-cost; prefer adaptive/conditional prefetch as fix.
Related internal tickets: INT-4543 (allocator profiling), INT-4590 (scheduler priority fix).
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround: disable KV prefetch at customer-level for LexiDocs dedicated pool (done for pool S-3 on 2026-03-12). Customer reported immediate improvement.

Medium-term fix: implement adaptive prefetch that checks memory headroom and generation CPU utilization before scheduling prefetch jobs (PR linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1892).
Long-term: revert kernel allocator thresholds or add slab-coalescing to reduce fragmentation for very large prefix allocations; tracked in INT-4701.

Rollout plan: canary in prod on 1 node for 48h, expand to 10% of pool after no regressions, full rollout in 7 days. Post-rollout monitoring: memory churn, slab_reclaim latency, 504 rate on long-context routes.
Customer communication: Maya to send change summary and expected timeline; offer temporary credits for runs impacted during investigation window.
Status: workaround applied, patch in review, canary scheduled.
